about: Engines the M0 benchmark (and later the apps) can use. Model ids live here, not in code. Prices in USD, checked 2026-10-26. rpm = requests per minute the benchmark allows itself (keep under the free tier). gemini-2.5-flash-lite was dropped on 2026-10-27: Google no longer offers it to new users. llama-3.1-8b-instant was replaced by openai/gpt-oss-120b on 2026-10-27: Groq no longer offers Llama 3.1 8B on standard keys. concurrency = requests the benchmark keeps in flight per provider (start times still follow rpm). default_engine = what the apps use out of the box (D-028; was groq-whisper-hint, D-011); fallback_engine = what they also ask when the default has not answered after a few seconds or failed (D-028). 2026-11-03: OpenAI added (gpt-4o-transcribe, paid, no free tier: prices from OpenAI's launch, ~$0.006 / $0.003 per minute); gemini-3.5-transcribe (preview, the Gemini app's dictation model; price as reported by third parties, $2 / $12 per 1M tokens) and gemini-3.5-flash (price not checked, so cost shows 0). gemini-3.8-flash was tried and dropped the same day: every request on the free tier timed out or got 503 "high demand". An engine's own rpm overrides the provider's. refine = a second, text-only step on another provider (prompt + chat model) after any engine. min_billed_s = the provider bills at least this many seconds per request (Groq: 10). catalog = what the model page shows (label, free / paid tier, free-tier limits with their source, notes); `python -m sonic_eval catalog` adds the benchmark results and writes spec/models.json.

catalog.label: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite

limits.text: Gemini free tier: about 10 requests/min, 500/day (third-party guide; Google shows the real numbers only in AI Studio). Not hit with 150+ requests in a day.

catalog.notes: Near the top for accuracy with a usable daily limit. Some requests take 10-20 s (Google's queue). Google may use free-tier requests to improve its products, and people may review them (Gemini API terms); the paid tier does not.

catalog.label: Groq Whisper (fast)

limits.text: Groq free tier: 20 requests/min, 2,000/day, 7,200 audio seconds/hour, 28,800 audio seconds/day (8 hours of speech)

catalog.notes: Fastest (~0.3 s) but weakest on natural Urdu / Hindi; writes text on silence (the voice gate stops that).

catalog.label: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe + Roman cleanup

limits.text: Gemini free tier: 25 requests/day (Google's own quota error, 2026-11-03), about 3-4/min (429 after 4 in a minute). Roman cleanup on Groq gpt-oss-20b (free tier: 30 requests/min, 1,000/day).

catalog.notes: The Gemini app's dictation model (preview). Hears Urdu / Hindi best but writes it in its own script, so a second step romanizes it; needs a Gemini and a Groq key. Paid: about $2 / $12 per 1M tokens (third-party reports). Google may use free-tier requests to improve its products, and people may review them (Gemini API terms); the paid tier does not.

catalog.label: Gemini 3.5 Flash

limits.text: Gemini free tier: 20 requests/day per project (Google's own quota error, 2026-11-03).

catalog.notes: Top accuracy, but 20 dictations a day on the free tier. Paid price not checked. Google may use free-tier requests to improve its products, and people may review them (Gemini API terms); the paid tier does not.

catalog.label: OpenAI GPT-4o Transcribe + Roman cleanup

limits.text: No free tier: about $0.006 per minute of audio. Roman cleanup on Groq gpt-oss-20b (free tier: 30 requests/min, 1,000/day).
limits.source: OpenAI pricing at launch; check before use

catalog.notes: Writes Urdu / Hindi script, so it needs the Roman cleanup; writes text on silence.

catalog.label: OpenAI GPT-4o mini Transcribe + Roman cleanup

limits.text: No free tier: about $0.003 per minute of audio. Roman cleanup on Groq gpt-oss-20b (free tier: 30 requests/min, 1,000/day).
limits.source: OpenAI pricing at launch; check before use

catalog.notes: Half the price of GPT-4o Transcribe and as accurate here; writes text on silence.
